title: Arabian and hook mates
line: A rook right next to the king, guarded by a knight, in the corner or out in the open.

steps.text: Arabian mate: the rook checks right next to the king in the corner. The knight guards the rook and takes the square the rook cannot.

steps.hint: The rook slides along its row to the square the knight guards.
steps.after: Checkmate. The king cannot take the rook, because the knight guards it.

steps.text: The same pair from the other side. Mate with the rook next to the king.
steps.hint: The rook goes up its open file to the back row.
steps.after: Checkmate. The knight guards the rook on g8, and Black's own pawn on h7 blocks the king.

steps.text: The hook mate: the rook checks next to the king, the knight guards the rook, and a pawn guards the knight and takes a square too.
Before you mate, tap the black pawn that blocks its own king.

wrong.h6: That pawn is not next to the king. Look at the squares around the black king.

steps.hint: Look at the squares right beside the black king.
steps.after: The pawn takes a square from its own king. Your rook, knight and pawn take the rest.

steps.hint: The rook slides along the back rank to the square the knight guards.
steps.after: Hook mate. The king cannot take the rook or the knight, and your pawn takes d6.

summary: A rook right next to the king, guarded by a knight that also takes a square, mates in the corner or in the open.
